Before the work, ask the right questions.

You do not need a perfect project file to get in touch. A few practical details can already help us understand your masonry, plastering, partitioning or tiling project. This guide helps prepare that conversation without turning an initial idea into a commitment.

Prepare our first conversation

Describe the result you want.

Start with the room and what is not working for you today. Do you want to divide a space, repair a wall, prepare surfaces or change a finish? Distinguish the elements to retain from those to alter. Note approximate dimensions and visible features of the substrate, without trying to make a technical diagnosis yourself.

  • Rooms involved and intended use
  • Approximate dimensions and elements to retain

Gather information about the property.

Give the project address, country and town. An existing plan and wider photographs, with close-ups of the surfaces where useful, can support the discussion. Avoid including unnecessary personal documents. Add the floor level, parking options, access routes, any lift and whether the home will remain occupied during the work.

  • Address and access conditions
  • Useful plans or views, if available

Prepare the questions to clarify in the quotation.

Explain your preferred timeframe and the constraints that matter to you. If you have a budget in mind or have already chosen materials, mention them to frame the conversation. Ask for clarity on the agreed work, materials, surface preparation, protection and finishing. The limits of the scope and work by other trades need to be identified before the project is accepted.

Before you begin.

Is the project summary prepared on the website a quotation?

No. The form prepares a local summary that you can download or open in your messaging app. It supports the first contact and does not provide a price or a commitment to carry out work.

Can I get in touch before my project is fully defined?

Yes. Describe what you would like to improve and which rooms are involved. We can start by clarifying your needs and the information required to assess the project.
